# tag: science.space.moon
how was the moon formed | where did the moon come from | how did the moon get there => Most scientists think the Moon formed about 4.5 billion years ago when a Mars-sized object called Theia smashed into the young Earth. The debris clumped into the Moon.
how old is the moon | age of the moon | how many years old is the moon => The Moon is about 4.5 billion years old, only a little younger than Earth.
what is the moon made of | is the moon made of rock | what are moon rocks made of => The Moon is made of rock, with a small iron core. Its surface is covered in a dusty layer called regolith.
how strong is gravity on the moon | how much would i weigh on the moon | moon gravity => Gravity on the Moon is about 1.6 m/s², around one sixth of Earth's. Someone who weighs 60 kg on Earth would feel like 10 kg there.
does the moon have an atmosphere | is there air on the moon | can you breathe on the moon => The Moon has almost no atmosphere, so there's no air to breathe and the sky is black even in daytime.
how hot is the moon | how cold is the moon | temperature on the moon => The Moon's surface gets to about 120 °C (250 °F) in sunlight and drops to about -130 °C (-208 °F) at night. Some dark craters are even colder.
why does the moon have craters | what made the craters on the moon | moon craters => Asteroids and comets hit the Moon over billions of years. With no air, wind or rain to wear them away, the craters stay for ages.
what are the dark spots on the moon | what are the maria on the moon | what is the man in the moon => The dark patches are called maria, Latin for seas. They're plains of old hardened lava, not water. People see faces or a rabbit in them.
is the moon moving away from earth | is the moon getting farther away | how fast is the moon drifting away => Yes. The Moon moves about 3.8 cm farther from Earth each year, about as fast as your fingernails grow.
how long does the moon take to orbit earth | how long is a lunar month | moon orbit time => The Moon orbits Earth in about 27.3 days. A full cycle of phases, from new moon to new moon, takes about 29.5 days.
is there water on the moon | does the moon have ice | water ice on the moon => Yes, there's water ice on the Moon, mostly hidden in very cold, always shadowed craters near the poles. That's why missions want to go to the south pole.
why is the moon sometimes out in the day | why can i see the moon during the day | moon in the daytime => The Moon is up during the day for part of most months. It's bright enough to see because it reflects sunlight, even when the sky is blue.
why does the moon look bigger near the horizon | what is the moon illusion | why is the moon huge tonight => That's the moon illusion. The Moon isn't actually bigger near the horizon. Your brain just judges its size differently when it's near trees and buildings.
what is a supermoon | why is the moon so big sometimes | supermoon meaning => A supermoon is a full moon that happens when the Moon is near its closest point to Earth. It looks up to about 14% bigger and 30% brighter than the smallest full moon.
what is a blue moon | is a blue moon really blue | once in a blue moon meaning => A blue moon usually means the second full moon in one calendar month. It isn't actually blue. It happens about every 2 to 3 years.
does the moon have earthquakes | what are moonquakes | are there moonquakes => Yes, the Moon has moonquakes. Seismometers left by the Apollo astronauts recorded them for years.
what is io | tell me about io moon | io jupiter moon => Io is one of Jupiter's four big moons. It's the most volcanic place in the solar system, with hundreds of active volcanoes.
why is io so volcanic | why does io have volcanoes | io volcanoes => Jupiter's huge gravity, plus tugs from the other moons, squeezes and stretches Io. That flexing heats its inside and powers its volcanoes.
what is europa | tell me about europa moon | europa jupiter moon => Europa is one of Jupiter's big moons, a bit smaller than our Moon. It's covered in ice, with a salty ocean underneath.
could there be life on europa | does europa have an ocean | is there water on europa => Europa likely has a salty ocean under its ice with about twice as much water as all of Earth's oceans. That makes it one of the best places to look for life.
what is europa clipper | europa clipper mission | when will europa clipper get to jupiter => Europa Clipper is a NASA spacecraft that launched in October 2024. It's set to reach Jupiter in 2030 and fly past Europa many times to study its ocean.
what is ganymede | what is the biggest moon in the solar system | largest moon => Ganymede, a moon of Jupiter, is the biggest moon in the solar system. At about 5,268 km wide, it's even bigger than the planet Mercury.
does ganymede have a magnetic field | ganymede facts | what is special about ganymede => Ganymede is the only moon known to have its own magnetic field. It probably has a salty ocean buried under its ice too.
what is callisto | callisto moon | tell me about callisto => Callisto is Jupiter's second biggest moon. It's one of the most heavily cratered objects in the solar system, and its surface is very old.
what are the galilean moons | who discovered jupiters moons | jupiters four big moons => The Galilean moons are Jupiter's four biggest moons: Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto. Galileo Galilei discovered them in 1610 with an early telescope.
what is the biggest moon of jupiter | jupiter biggest moon | largest moon of jupiter => Ganymede is Jupiter's biggest moon, and the biggest moon in the whole solar system.
what is titan | tell me about titan moon | titan saturn moon => Titan is Saturn's biggest moon and the second biggest in the solar system. It's the only moon with a thick atmosphere.
does titan have lakes | what are the lakes on titan made of | is there liquid on titan => Yes, Titan has lakes and seas, but they're filled with liquid methane and ethane, not water. It even rains methane there.
who discovered titan | when was titan discovered | who found saturns moon titan => Christiaan Huygens discovered Titan in 1655.
what is dragonfly | dragonfly mission to titan | nasa drone to titan => Dragonfly is a NASA drone, like a car sized quadcopter, planned to fly around Titan. As of 2025, it's set to launch in 2028.
what is the biggest moon of saturn | saturn biggest moon | largest moon of saturn => Titan is Saturn's biggest moon. It's bigger than the planet Mercury.
what is enceladus | tell me about enceladus | enceladus geysers => Enceladus is a small, icy moon of Saturn. It shoots geysers of water vapor and ice from cracks near its south pole, from an ocean underneath.
could there be life on enceladus | does enceladus have an ocean | is there water on enceladus => Enceladus has a salty ocean under its ice. Cassini flew through its spray and found water, salt and simple organic chemicals, so it's a top place to search for life.
what is mimas | why does mimas look like the death star | mimas moon => Mimas is a small moon of Saturn with a giant crater called Herschel. The crater makes it look a lot like the Death Star from Star Wars.
what is iapetus | why is iapetus two colors | iapetus moon => Iapetus is a moon of Saturn with one side dark as coal and the other bright as snow. It also has a strange ridge around its middle.
what is triton | tell me about triton | neptunes biggest moon => Triton is Neptune's biggest moon. It orbits backward, which means it was probably a captured object from the Kuiper belt. It has geysers of nitrogen.
who discovered triton | when was triton discovered | who found neptunes moon => William Lassell discovered Triton in 1846, just 17 days after Neptune itself was discovered.
what is charon | plutos biggest moon | how big is charon => Charon is Pluto's biggest moon, about 1,212 km wide, roughly half the size of Pluto. They face each other with the same side all the time.
what is phobos | tell me about phobos | is phobos going to crash into mars => Phobos is the bigger of Mars's two moons, about 22 km wide and lumpy like a potato. It's slowly spiraling inward and will break apart or crash in about 50 million years.
what is deimos | tell me about deimos | mars smaller moon => Deimos is the smaller of Mars's two moons, only about 12 km wide. Both moons were discovered by Asaph Hall in 1877.
what are the moons of mars called | names of mars moons | phobos and deimos meaning => Mars's moons are Phobos and Deimos, which mean fear and panic in Greek. They're named after the sons of Ares, the Greek god of war.
what is miranda | miranda moon of uranus | what is the biggest cliff in the solar system => Miranda is a small moon of Uranus with a jumbled surface. It has Verona Rupes, a cliff about 20 km tall, one of the tallest known.
what is the biggest moon of uranus | what is titania | uranus biggest moon => Titania is the biggest moon of Uranus, about 1,577 km wide. Uranus's moons are named after characters from Shakespeare and Alexander Pope.
why are uranus moons named after shakespeare | how are uranus moons named | uranus moon names => Uranus's moons are named after characters from Shakespeare plays and Alexander Pope's poem, like Titania, Oberon, Miranda, Ariel and Puck.
